snapshot_auto.quote:
Upon completion of the
build, volumes and their contents are discarded.
snapshot_auto.note: Job-scoped ephemeral build workers; nothing is saved when a build ends (only pushed images/artifacts and optional caches you upload yourself).

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Cloud Build is a service that executes your builds on Google Cloud.
snapshot_on_demand.note: No snapshot/checkpoint API anywhere in the Cloud Build API reference or docs for build workers; consistent with snapshot='none'.

harness_api.quote: For each build step, Cloud Build executes a Docker container as an instance of docker run.
harness_api.note: No first-party API to drive a coding-agent harness (prompt/stream events/follow-ups) inside a build; you could run a CLI tool as a generic build step, but that is not a harness API.

egress_allowlist.quote:
Remove public IPs on private pools by setting egressOption field in the private pool config file to NO_PUBLIC_EGRESS.
This will remove all access from the private pool to the public internet.
egress_allowlist.note: Private pools only (default pool always has internet). Options: NO_PUBLIC_EGRESS (no-internet mode, gcloud --no-public-egress), VPC Service Controls perimeter, and 'Customize firewall rules on your VPC network to restrict egress' on the peered VPC (IP/CIDR/port). Per pool, not per build; enforced outside the worker.

ingress_rules.quote: its own worker and is isolated from other workloads.
ingress_rules.note: Build workers expose no inbound ports/URLs at all, so there is nothing to control (not a 'public with no controls' case). The VPC-SC 'ingress policy' in the docs governs who may call the Cloud Build API, not traffic to workers.

secret_proxy.quote:
env: a local name (environment variable) that build steps can use to
reference the secret.
secret_proxy.note: Secret Manager secrets (availableSecrets / secretEnv) and KMS-encrypted secrets are injected as environment variables into build steps; no credential-injecting proxy.

volume_attach.quote:
Each volume is created
as an empty volume prior to starting the build process. Upon completion of the
build, volumes and their contents are discarded.
volume_attach.note: Only per-build Docker volumes shared between steps and a configurable diskSizeGb; no persistent/attachable volumes.

volume_shared.quote:
is a Docker container volume that is mounted into build steps to persist files
across build steps.
volume_shared.note: Build volumes are shared only between sequential steps of the same build on one worker; no cross-worker shared filesystem (use GCS/Filestore over the network yourself).

isolation.quote: we are the largest submitter of CVEs and security bug fixes for the Linux KVM hypervisor.
isolation.note: Each Cloud Build runs on its own dedicated Compute Engine worker VM ('Each build runs on its own worker and is isolated from other workloads', private-pools-overview) sized by GCE machine type (e2/n2d/c3); Google's infrastructure docs confirm KVM is the underlying hypervisor for its compute fleet. Exact hypervisor is not named per-product, so classified as full VM (qemu-kvm) rather than microVM.

image_oci.quote: Use the name field of a build step to specify a cloud builder, which is a container image running common tools. You use a builder in a build step to execute your tasks.
image_oci.note: Every build step runs an arbitrary container image (name: field) pulled from any registry, including custom/private Docker or OCI images you publish yourself; oci artifacts are also natively supported for output.

nested_virt.note: Cloud Build's own workflow for producing VM images (e.g. with Packer) delegates to the Compute Engine API to create real GCE instances rather than emulating a VM locally inside the build step; no docs mention /dev/kvm or nested virtualization being exposed to build containers.

browser.quote: Cloud Build lets you build software quickly across all languages... on VMs (or on Kubernetes, or serverless).
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (CI build service that runs container-based build steps, not a browser/computer-use product).

anti_bot.quote: Cloud Build lets you build software quickly across all languages... on VMs (or on Kubernetes, or serverless).
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

captcha_solving.quote: Cloud Build lets you build software quickly across all languages... on VMs (or on Kubernetes, or serverless).
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

egress_ip_type.quote: you must set up a virtual machine (VM) in your project to act as a self-managed NAT gateway to proxy requests to the public internet.
egress_ip_type.note: Default pool builds egress from Google's shared datacenter IP ranges; a fixed/static IP on private pools requires the customer to build and operate their own self-managed NAT gateway VM, so out-of-the-box egress is shared datacenter IPs, not provider-managed static IPs.

ssh.quote: Access GitHub from a build via SSH keys
ssh.note: Cloud Build's SSH-related docs are about builds using SSH keys to reach source repos (e.g. GitHub), not interactive SSH access into the build worker itself; it's a batch CI job runner with no documented shell/SSH login to the worker VM.

own_agent_api.quote: Cloud Build lets you build software quickly across all languages... on VMs (or on Kubernetes, or serverless).
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (CI/CD build automation, not a browser/computer-use task agent).

egress_http_rules.quote: Customize firewall rules on your VPC network to restrict egress ... Remove public IPs on private pools by setting egressOption field in the private pool config file to NO_PUBLIC_EGRESS.
egress_http_rules.note: Egress control on private pools is all-or-nothing (NO_PUBLIC_EGRESS) or VPC firewall/VPC-SC rules at IP/CIDR/port level; nothing at HTTP method/path granularity.

guest_firewall.quote: Each build runs on its own worker and is isolated from other workloads.
guest_firewall.note: derived: full VM worker with root access inside the build container/VM, so iptables/nftables configuration inside the guest is expected to work.

static_egress_ip.quote: This page explains how you can set up your private pools to access external resources through a static external IP.
static_egress_ip.note: Achievable on private pools by routing egress through a self-managed NAT gateway VM you create in your VPC; not an automatic per-machine static IP assigned by the provider out of the box.

max_session_h.quote: The maximum value for timeout is 24 hours.
max_session_h.note: Overall build timeout field is capped at 24 hours; individual build steps can have shorter timeouts.

persistent_disk.quote: Each volume is created as an empty volume prior to starting the build process. Upon completion of the build, volumes and their contents are discarded.
persistent_disk.note: Build workers are ephemeral per-build; the workspace and any declared volumes are wiped when the build finishes. No first-party mechanism keeps a worker's filesystem across builds.

snapshot.quote: Upon completion of the build, volumes and their contents are discarded.
snapshot.note: No disk or memory snapshot/checkpoint concept exists for build workers; state is either discarded or you push it yourself (image/artifact/GCS).

pause_resume.quote: Cloud Build is a service that executes your builds on Google Cloud.
pause_resume.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Cloud Build runs a single job-to-completion build on an ephemeral worker; there is no pause/resume lifecycle for a build (only cancel).

fork.quote: Cloud Build is a service that executes your builds on Google Cloud.
fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. A build worker is a one-shot execution environment for a single build, not a machine you clone.

fork_running.quote: Cloud Build is a service that executes your builds on Google Cloud.
fork_running.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (no fork capability at all, running or otherwise).

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Cloud Build is a service that executes your builds on Google Cloud.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (no fork or memory-snapshot capability exists).

desktop.quote: Cloud Build uses Docker to execute builds. For each build step, Cloud Build executes a Docker container as an instance of docker run.
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Build steps are headless Docker container runs; there is no graphical desktop/VNC/RDP surface.

computer_use.quote: Cloud Build uses Docker to execute builds. For each build step, Cloud Build executes a Docker container as an instance of docker run.
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No desktop exists, so there is no screenshot/click API to drive one.

wake_on_request.quote: Cloud Build is a service that executes your builds on Google Cloud.
wake_on_request.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Builds are triggered (API call/trigger/repo push) and spin up a fresh worker; there is no persistent/sleeping machine that 'wakes' since none stays around between builds.

volumes.quote: A Volume is a Docker container volume that is mounted into build steps to persist files across build steps... Upon completion of the build, volumes and their contents are discarded.
volumes.note: Only ephemeral, per-build Docker volumes shared between sequential steps of the same build; nothing persistent or attachable across builds/workers.

inbound_https.quote: its own worker and is isolated from other workloads.
inbound_https.note: Build workers expose no inbound ports or URLs; they run steps and exit. Nothing to reach via HTTPS.

public_ipv4.quote: Cloud Build is a service that executes your builds on Google Cloud.
public_ipv4.note: Build workers are not addressable machines with a public IPv4 assigned to the customer; they only make outbound calls (pull source/images, push artifacts). Consistent with card's network.ipv4_available: false.

agent_harnesses.quote: Cloud Build uses Docker to execute builds. For each build step, Cloud Build executes a Docker container as an instance of docker run.
agent_harnesses.note: No preinstalled/offered coding-agent (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode) templates in Cloud Build's build-step catalog; it only provides generic community/Google container build steps.

mcp_server.quote: Cloud Build is a service that executes your builds on Google Cloud.
mcp_server.note: No provider-shipped MCP server to control Cloud Build workers found in the docs.

gpu.quote: default pool e2-standard-2 2 vCPU/8 GB ... private pools E2 standard ... N2D/C3 private-pool machine types
gpu.note: Pricing page lists only E2/N2D/C3 CPU machine families for build workers; no GPU worker option is offered.

windows.quote: Cloud Build uses Docker to execute builds. For each build step, Cloud Build executes a Docker container as an instance of docker run. Currently, Cloud Build is running Docker engine version 20.10.24.
windows.note: Build workers run Linux Docker containers only; no Windows build-worker option is offered.

macos.quote: Cloud Build uses Docker to execute builds. For each build step, Cloud Build executes a Docker container as an instance of docker run.
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Cloud Build only runs Linux Docker-container build steps; no macOS workers exist on Google Cloud.

arm64.quote: default pool e2-standard-2 ... private pools E2 standard ... N2D/C3 private-pool machine types
arm64.note: All listed default/private-pool worker machine types (E2, N2D, C3) are x86-64 GCE families; no Arm (Tau T2A) worker option is listed on the pricing page or in the private pools docs.

self_host.quote: Cloud Build is a service that executes your builds on Google Cloud.
self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Cloud Build is a fully managed Google-run service; there is no self-hosted/on-prem distribution of the build execution service itself.

byoc.quote: its own worker and is isolated from other workloads.
byoc.note: Private pools let build workers peer into your own VPC network, but the workers themselves still run in Google-managed infrastructure/projects, not deployed as a managed service into an arbitrary customer cloud account (not AWS/Azure BYOC).

open_source.quote: Cloud Build is a service that executes your builds on Google Cloud.
open_source.note: Cloud Build is a proprietary managed Google Cloud service; no OSI-licensed core product is published for it.

live_resize.quote: options: machineType: enum(MachineType) ... diskSizeGb: string (int64 format)
live_resize.note: machineType/diskSizeGb are set per-build in the config file before the worker starts; there is no API to change CPU/RAM of an already-running build worker.

usage_api.quote: Billing export to BigQuery provides detailed information on resource labels and tags, allowing you to filter Cloud Build costs by user_labels or default labels set on individual builds
usage_api.note: granularity: per-tag; cost: yes; Cloud Build billing is accessible via Google Cloud's standard Billing Export API (BigQuery) and Cost Explorer API (with resource filtering by labels/tags). Individual builds can be tagged with custom labels (user_labels) in the build config, and billing data can be filtered by these labels and the Cloud Build service. Costs are returned in currency, not just usage quantities. The Billing API/export breaks down costs per build via resource labels and supports querying by build properties.

locations_quote: Cloud Build allows you to run regional builds by specifying the region when starting a build or when creating a build trigger. All listed regions support both default and private pools.
